name: Raymond Ltd
title: Raymond Ltd - 500330 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.9% (up from 15.7%); aerospace revenue +40% YoY to INR123 cr but margin fell to 21.2% from 23.7% on expensed R&D; capacity-led growth with a 2 yr-plus greenfield ramp.

summary.headline: Raymond Q1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 13% to INR628 crores, with EBITDA up 14% to INR100 crores at a 15.9% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR628 crores (up 13% YoY) and EBITDA reached INR100 crores (up 14% YoY) at a 15.9% margin, versus 15.7% a year earlier. Aerospace (JKMGAL) revenue grew 40% to INR123 crores, but its EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% from 23.7% because R&D for new programmes was expensed in the quarter. Precision Technology and Auto Components (JKMPTL) revenue grew 11% to INR444 crores, with EBITDA up 46% to INR61 crores and margin expanding to 13.8% from 10.6%, driven by export ramp-up and operating leverage. Management reiterated a 25% organic growth commitment for aerospace and plans for an aftermarket business launching in Q2 FY27 and a greenfield facility in Andhra Pradesh targeting commercial production in late 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +13% YoY (vs INR555 crores in Q1 FY26)
+14% YoY (vs INR87 crores in Q1 FY26)
Company stated it remains net debt-free

segments.name: Aerospace & Defence (JKMGAL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR123 crores (+40% YoY) and EBITDA INR26 crores at 21.2% margin, down from 23.7%, due to expensed R&D for new programmes. Order book of INR5,960 crores over 10 years and RFQ pipeline of INR1,632 crores; mass production of precision defence components has commenced.

segments.name: Precision Technology & Auto Components (JKMPTL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR444 crores (+11% YoY), led by export ramp-up, with EBITDA INR61 crores at 13.8% margin (vs 10.6%). Automotive aftermarket product line scheduled for launch in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Aerospace: committed 25% organic growth for the year; management said it is slightly ahead of that in Q1.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to follow the current trend, per management's answer on FY27 margins (analyst had cited a 12-13% range).
Aerospace mature EBITDA margin target around 25%; precision manufacturing around 12-13% in the near and medium term.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield facility (Gudipalli, near Bangalore Airport) targeted for commercial production in late 2027; up to 6 months of approvals, so meaningful revenue from FY28.
Existing aerospace facility now expected to exceed the earlier INR600 crore revenue estimate, per the Parivartan improvement programme.
Asset turns on new business: aerospace about 1.8-2.2x, automotive about 2-2.5x; ROCE expected to be broadly maintained.
Aftermarket business for automotive components and white-label products to roll out in Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: INR1,000 crore five-year capex plan: INR510 crores for aerospace and INR430 crores for auto; management says it is progressing on schedule.
Greenfield Andhra Pradesh facility (Gudipalli, near Bangalore Airport) groundwork on track; commercial production targeted for late 2027.
Setting up an advanced training and production facility near the greenfield site ahead of schedule for pre-launch readiness.
Plans to add special processes such as heat treatment at the Andhra facility to increase vertical integration.
Current aerospace order book relates only to the existing facility; new capacity is over a year away.
demand_pricing: Aerospace demand described as well ahead of supply; management said supply chain constraints (titanium, alloys) eased in Q1 but cited a large backlog.
Export revival for auto components helped by the India-UK CETA (in force 15 July 2026) and the rollback of US tariffs; Tier 1 buyers rebuilding inventory.
Aerospace customer concentration: over 25 global customers, with top 3 at about 40-45% of the business. Management aims to widen this to 8-10 high-value customers.
Input costs rising: logistics, carbide and HSS tooling, and minimum wage increases. Some costs are being passed to customers; management expects some quarterly pressure.
Management said it had N4 self-certification and that engine-critical parts are the core; it is not yet in N1 (rotating parts).

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity for inorganic deals after the warrant issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it keeps evaluating inorganic opportunities across aerospace, auto components and defence; the warrants give flexibility, and it will update only when deals are close.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to aerospace casting and forging supply bottlenecks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exposed as much because critical-part programmes have not yet transferred; the constraint is seen as an execution advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Will consolidated EBITDA margins stay around 12-13% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the same trend as shown in Q1 at consolidated level, with margins better than last year.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the 10-year aerospace order book versus the earlier 5-year figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The change was made to give longer visibility; the 5-year breakup summed to about INR2,765 crores versus INR2,350 crores last quarter, which an analyst computed as about 17% QoQ growth, and management confirmed this. The INR5,960 crore book covers only the existing facility.

qa_highlights.question: How much can the existing facility produce, and what is the timeline for the new facility revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing facility is expected to exceed the earlier INR600 crore estimate under the Parivartan programme. New facility revenue starts in FY28 after up to 6 months of approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What are asset turns and long-term margin targets by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace new business asset turns of 1.8-2.2x and auto 2-2.5x. Long-term EBITDA margin targets are about 25% for aerospace and 12-13% for precision manufacturing.

risks_watch: Aerospace margin (21.2%, down 2.5 pp YoY) depends on R&D write-offs and product maturity; management expects stabilisation as programmes move to steady state.
Rising input costs (tooling, logistics, wages) may compress margins for a quarter before pass-through or efficiency offsets.
Customer concentration: top 3 aerospace customers at about 40-45%.
Greenfield ramp depends on customer approvals (up to 6 months); late 2027 start with FY28 revenue impact.
Inorganic deals are not yet identified, and the warrant issue means possible dilution if deals close.
Medical certification obtained, but no business plan yet; defence strategy under development after hiring a former BEL executive.
